gaps.lead: The committee probably won't change the rules.
gaps.sentence: ___ the committee will change the rules.
gaps.explanation: probably won't = it is (highly) unlikely that.

gaps.lead: Although the traffic was heavy, we reached the airport in time.
gaps.sentence: We reached the airport in time ___ traffic.
gaps.explanation: 'Although the traffic was heavy' becomes 'despite the heavy traffic' — despite + noun phrase.

gaps.lead: I don't expect the company to make a profit this year, given the economic climate.
gaps.sentence: Given the economic climate, ___ the company made a profit this year.
gaps.hint: don't expect = would be surprised if + past
gaps.explanation: A tentative prediction: 'I would be surprised if + past simple'.

gaps.lead: The plane left the runway moments before the storm hit.
gaps.sentence: The plane had ___ the storm hit.
gaps.explanation: had just + participle = a moment before.

gaps.lead: She hates it when people interrupt her.
Someone must check this equipment before every flight.
gaps.explanation: must check → must be checked (modal + be + past participle).

gaps.lead: They cancelled the match because of the rain.
gaps.sentence: The match ___ because of the rain.

gaps.lead: It isn't necessary to book in advance.
gaps.explanation: 'Don't have to' = it is not necessary.
